title: data audit does not run content findings, so percent-on-zero-baseline passes the gate
reason: tools/data.py _audit_command never calls _collect_findings. A percent modifier on a stat whose actor_stats baseline is 0.0 resolves to (0.0+0)*(1+p) = 0.0, i.e. a silent no-op, but 'data audit' reports clean. Only 'data distribution' catches it, via _resolve_zero_baseline_stats(), and distribution is non-gating by default. Found by the wave-49 J14 agent on four items.

title: 120 qi dantian/meridian catalysts are orphaned: recipe-produced but consumed by nothing and not exempt from the modifier-coverage check
reason: tools/generate_qi_items.py:240-241 emits qi_<realm>_dantian_catalyst and qi_<realm>_meridian_catalyst, but no realm seed declares a dantian_catalyst or meridian_catalyst field (seed fields are only breakthrough_item, training_item, sea_catalyst, strengthening_item, dantian_tier, sea_tier, required_channel_state). _progression_items() exempts an item by finding it referenced in a seed field whose name ends in _item/_catalyst, so these 120 are never exempt: they carry no modifiers (correct for a progression payload per ADR 0009) yet trip 'consumable has 90 items with no modifiers'. title: 24 legacy chains use a 4-stage shape (base/refined/anointed/perfected) while 334 others use the 5-stage shape
reason: The J1_-J24_ chain family is built as base -> refined -> anointed -> perfected with a 3-value modifier ladder (0.04/0.07/0.14), whereas every other chain in the corpus is base/refined/aged/primed/perfected with 0.03/0.06/0.09/0.13/0.17. A stem-based verifier that assumes the 5-stage shape classifies these 24 as broken (missing aged and primed), which is wrong - they resolve and audit clean. Consequences: their capstones top out at 0.14 instead of 0.17, and the J-chains never got the dual refined/aged alt routes the 5-stage chains have.
next: Decide whether to normalise the J family or declare it a supported second shape. Normalising is NOT possible with the sanctioned tooling: data edit cannot change a recipe's inputs or delete a recipe, so it would mean deleting and recreating 96 items and 72 recipes by hand. If it stays, teach the shape-aware verifiers to detect the 4-stage family explicitly instead of inferring shape from a suffix list.

title: 11 subtypes with <=4 items are deliberate narrative one-offs, not thin categories - do not generate packs for them

They are hand-authored seed props, each pinned to a specific narrative source: quest_ancient_map is quest:main_03, quest_beast_fang is quest:side_02, quest_cultivation_manual is quest:side_04, quest_sealed_letter is quest:main_01, quest_spirit_stone_shard is quest:side_03, curr_chaos_shard drops from boss:E10_dao_warden, curr_primordial_mark from boss:E10_transcendent_oracle, and currency_seal_token / currency_tribute_scroll both sit on quest:A37_route. Any future thin-subtype targeting must exclude subtypes whose items carry a hard quest:<id> or boss:<id> reference, since that is the signature of a narrative one-off. Only quest/token (3 items, no pinned source) is a genuine candidate for growth.

title: The material-pack brief's 'starved subtypes' list is stale prose - do not target it, and prefer genuinely NEW subtypes instead
source: wave 71 E13 agent flag, confirmed by disk measurement
reason: chaos-content-brief-material61.md tells agents to draw from a fixed set of eight starved subtypes (tablet, scroll, gemstone, ingot, fragment, core, filament, bone). Measured on disk, all eight already hold 71-112 items each (tablet 88, scroll 90, gemstone 112, ingot 112, fragment 91, core 94, filament 71, bone 107) - none is starved. A wave-71 agent read that prose, noticed its assigned subtype was not on the list, and correctly reported the pack would not relieve the gap it named. It was following the right instinct against a wrong instruction: the pack's actual job was to refill the unconsumed gather pool, which it did, and it additionally took material subtypes from 15 to 19 by using four genuinely new ones (bark, horn, pearl, gut).
next: When cutting a material pack, prefer a subtype that does not exist yet over a thin one that does - a new subtype raises the subtype count, a thin one only adds depth. Ignore any hardcoded subtype list in the brief prose; measure thinness from disk with tools data distribution or a direct count. The same brief also has a second stale claim: it says lines are --sources gather while some per-line task files say quest. Where the two disagree the per-line task file wins, and only gather puts a material into the unconsumed pool that chains draw from.

title: 127 duplicate display names are legacy id-stem collisions needing an item-identity ruling, not an automatic rename
reason: 187 names are duplicated across 239 excess items. They split three ways. (1) 46 groups are all-material and benign: accessory_gale_essence, armor_gale_essence, belt_gale_essence and six more are nine separate items that all legitimately read 'Gale Essence' - same concept, and renaming them to variants would be strictly worse, so leave them. (2) 1 group is a real defect: U13_divine_scupper_base/refined/aged/primed/perfected all display as 'Divine Scupper Manual', so a five-stage crafting chain is indistinguishable by name. (3) 140 groups are genuinely distinct items sharing a name, and these trace to legacy seed generators colliding - H1_earth_breakthrough_pill, btchance_earth_pill and elemental_earth_breakthrough_pill are three different items, all earth grade, all named 'Earth Breakthrough Pill'. Only 13 of the 140 are disambiguated by grade alone. The other 127 need a second discriminator, and picking one means ruling on which item IS the canonical breakthrough pill and what the other two are - an item-identity decision, not a rename.
next: Wave 72 fixes the deterministic subset: the 1 chain-stages group and the 13 grade-unique groups, using the grade prefix that 5322 of 7273 existing names already follow. Leave the 46 benign material groups alone. The remaining 127 need an explicit ruling first: decide the canonical item per colliding name, then either rename the losers to reflect what they actually are or delete them as duplicates. Do not delegate that ruling to content-generation agents - they will improvise inconsistent discriminators.

title: ADR 0025 migration left tools/data.py blind to every modifier - audit clean is meaningless and authored stat-set diversity was erased
source: wave 72 verification after the ADR 0025 corpus migration landed mid-wave
reason: ADR 0025 Accepted 2026-10-02 replaced ItemDef stub flat_modifiers and percent_modifiers with fixed_modifiers holding a master option id plus value, and a roll_spec, then migrated the corpus. 7950 of 7950 item files now carry fixed_modifiers and roll_spec and zero carry the old maps. Three consequences. First, the gate is blind - tools/data.py line 44 still declares dicts as flat_modifiers and percent_modifiers only, and every audit and distribution rule reads those two keys, so the audit sees zero modifiers corpus-wide and reports data audit clean while validating nothing, and tools data distribution prints Modifier Stat Distribution none plus 34 declared stats never used by any item, which is false since it is all 34. A clean audit is no longer evidence of anything. Second, authored diversity was destroyed rather than migrated - a wave-72 five-stat item authored as breakthrough_chance plus evasion plus fortune plus penetration plus physique at three-decimal percents now reads fixed_modifiers with a single base_comprehension option at integer value 6 and roll_spec count 1, so the stat-combination and modifier-value diversity built across waves 69 to 72, including 100 percent stat-pair coverage, 142 distinct three-stat sets and 81 distinct percent values, is no longer present in the data. Third, tools/data.py still emits the dead schema, since _new_command writes percent_modifiers and flat_modifiers, so any item created with data new --percent lands in the legacy shape while the corpus is in the new one. HEAD item_def.gd still accepts both shapes through build_fixed_modifiers, which is why 4849 of 4890 tests pass. tools/item_migrate.py, the tool that rewrote all 7950 files, is still untracked.
next: Do not dispatch item-generation agents until tools/data.py is taught the ADR 0025 schema: add fixed_modifiers and roll_spec to the parsed dicts, rewrite every modifier rule to read them, and either teach _new_command to emit fixed_modifiers and roll_spec or document that new items are still authored in the legacy shape. Until then do not cite data audit clean as evidence, and treat the tools data distribution modifier sections as non-functional. Separately decide whether the authored stat-set programme is retired under ADR 0025 - if it is, waves 69 to 72 need a target expressed in option-pool membership, roll budget and rarity/realm pairing rather than authored stat combinations.

title: ADR 0025 catalog eligibility is category-scoped and far too narrow - 99.4 percent of authored stat diversity was silently discarded on migration
source: wave 72 survival measurement against the ADR 0025 catalog
reason: ADR 0025 replaces authored stat maps with master-catalog option references, and the catalog is far narrower than the stat vocabulary the corpus uses, so authored diversity is discarded rather than migrated. Measured over wave 72 own 344 non-material items: of 501 stat tokens encoded in their ids, only 3 survive as fixed_modifiers options, a 0.6 percent survival rate. Per item, 242 lost every authored stat, 101 lost some, and 1 kept all. The cause is category-scoped eligibility. The catalog holds 107 options over 92 stats, but eligibility is narrow and unequal: equipment gets 93 options over 92 stats, technique gets 36, material gets 5, and consumable gets only 9 - awareness, body_integrity, desire, essence, health, mind_power, qi, stamina and tribulation_essence. Those 9 consumable options are resource pools, not combat stats, so a consumable item can no longer carry a combat modifier at all. Every one of the 184 consumable items in this wave now grants health via the restore_health category default instead of its authored effect. tools/item_migrate.py drops any stat whose option is ineligible or missing with no warning, and then substitutes CATEGORY_FIXED, so the loss is silent.
next: Decide the programme target before another wave. Authored stat-combination diversity is void under ADR 0025: pair coverage, three and four and five stat sets, and novel modifier values cannot survive migration for consumable items and mostly cannot for technique items. The expressible axes are now option-pool membership, roll budget where count comes from rarity via RARITY_COUNT common 1 magic 2 rare 3 legendary 4, rarity and realm pairing, and category eligibility coverage. Two things need an owner decision. First, whether consumable items are meant to carry combat stats at all, since the current catalog says they cannot and the corpus says they always did. Second, whether the catalog should be widened so technique and consumable have real option coverage. Until that is settled, target equipment only, where all 92 stats are eligible. Separately, tools/data.py still parses only flat_modifiers and percent_modifiers, so data audit and data distribution cannot see any modifier and a clean audit is not evidence.

title: tools/item_migrate.py is broken and untracked - missing import zlib makes the only sanctioned ADR 0025 migration path unrunnable
source: wave 73 end-to-end schema probe in an isolated temp root
reason: tools/item_migrate.py is the only sanctioned path from authored stat maps to ADR 0025 option references, and it cannot run. Line 164 calls zlib.crc32 inside realm_for, but the module imports only re, pathlib.Path and two local modules - there is no import zlib anywhere in the file. Every run dies on the first item with NameError: name zlib is not defined, confirmed against an isolated temp root and against the real corpus with --limit 1. The file is also untracked with no git history at all, so the migration that rewrote all 7950 item files cannot be reproduced from anything in the repository and the working state of the tool is unknown. Consequence: nobody can author new-schema content, and nobody can re-run or verify the corpus migration.
next: Add import zlib to tools/item_migrate.py - that single line is the whole fix, and the tool then runs in dry-run by default so it is safe to validate before --apply. Then commit the tool, because until it is tracked the corpus migration is unreproducible. After that, verify the migration is faithful by re-running it in dry run and confirming it reports zero changes, which also proves the 7950 already-migrated files are stable under it. Only then re-target generation, per DEF-0048.

title: Body items use 4 of the 6 grades; seed.py keys grade off tier not realm
reason: The taxonomy declares 6 grades (mortal, spirit, earth, heaven, immortal, divine) but seed.py picks the grade from the realm TIER, so all body content resolves to mortal/spirit/immortal/divine and earth/heaven are never used. The grade axis carries no information beyond tier for body items.
next: Either grade body items across 6 bands so the axis is live, or record in ADR 0028 that body content collapses the 6 grades onto the 4 tiers deliberately.

title: Tribulation is inert: advance_wave has no production caller
reason: Resolved, and the audit was right in a way that understated it. Nothing in src called advance_wave, so no high-tier gate could ever be satisfied in play. Added Breakthrough.begin_tribulation/advance_tribulation/resolve_tribulation/cancel_tribulation in core (not on three module facades: ui already depends on core, and pushing begin onto all three would have breached the 12-method ISP cap). Supplying the entry points exposed two further defects, both fixed in ADR 0041: tribulation_ok asked only is_complete(), so a fight that ran to its last phase but was never decided opened the gate and _apply_failure stayed unreachable; and apply_result cleared actor.tribulation, so a decided win vanished on the next save and silently re-closed the gate it had earned. A tribulation now carries an explicit outcome and is durable.
next: Nothing. 10 tests in tests/core/test_tribulation_entry.gd cover begin/advance/resolve/cancel, one-survivor-one-realm, no restart of an unfinished fight, and survivor plus in-progress resume across a save round trip.

title: Cultivation UI: costs and rewards are not surfaced, and the mind screen is still unbuilt
reason: All cultivation screen work was deferred while the ui/ program was rebuilt from scratch by another agent. The rebuild has since landed qi_cultivation_screen and a shared action_bar, so the no-qi-panel gap is closed. What remains is that the objective names 8 UI fields and only 5 are surfaced: neither panel_state exposes a costs or rewards key, and the body panel's acupoint/channel read is the only meridian view. Gameplay contracts are already published, so the UI only needs to consume them: BodyCultivationApi.panel_state/recover_next and QiCultivationApi.panel_state/attempt_breakthrough/meditate/recover_next, with per-realm step sizes in each facade (STEPS). Note ui/ is at the 12-method facade cap for items and body_cultivation, so a new need there means splitting the facade, not growing it.
next: Add costs and rewards keys to both panel_state dictionaries, and close DEF-0035 for the mind screen. Every screen and panel exposes summary() and never reads a module internal.

title: Realm rewards are a flat constant on every realm seed - a balance decision, not missing mechanics
reason: qi grants {spirit: 2.0} and mind {will: 2.0} on all 30 realms each, against a now-measured power ladder of P=1.00 to 601.43 (ADR 0016). The mechanic is correct and transactional - the award is granted exactly once per resolved attempt and survives save/load - but the magnitude is unauthored, so a R1 pill and a R30 pill grant the same amount. This is a tuning decision about how reward should scale, not an unfinished feature.
next: Still needs an owner ruling on whether realm rewards scale with power or stay flat by design; the mechanic itself is correct and transactional. The shared power ladder this used to point at is gone (superseded by ADR 0050) - do NOT reintroduce it. If the owner rules that rewards scale, the scale to read is the authored per-realm multiplier in core/realm_power_table.tres (keyed by realm id), not a computed curve, and rewards stay flat-by-default until then. Assert monotonic growth in cultivation validate once ruled.

title: Mind power-curve tests still assert the removed RealmDef.power scaling
reason: Obsolete, and honestly so. The two assertions it names now pass because they were REWRITTEN, not because the ladder came back. ADR 0042 replaced the removed derived RealmDef.power with the authored per-realm table core/realm_power_table.tres (ADR 0050), but test_mind_path.gd no longer reads either: 'rank 10 scales' and 'sense range' both derive their expected value from MindRealmProfile.factor() - this path's own bounded RATE - via the suite's own _rate() helper, so they pin a rate and cannot go stale against a magnitude retune. The deferral's suggested fix (rebuild the expecteds from PowerLadder) would have been WRONG: it would have pinned a shared magnitude into a provider that must not read one (see test_mind_power_curve.gd's no-double-count rule). Verified: test_mind_path 9 passed, 0 failed.

title: Tribulation preparation can never reduce difficulty: start() clears preparation after computing it
reason: Tribulation._compute_difficulty reads actor preparation to lower the rating, but start() sets preparation = {} AFTER calling it, so the branch can only ever see the previous tribulation's stale preparation. Found while replacing PowerLadder in the difficulty formula (ADR 0050); left as-is because clearing preparation first is a design decision about when preparation is entered, not a refactor.
next: Decide whether preparation is an input to difficulty (then start() must read it before clearing, or preparation must be entered after start) or a mid-trial reduction (then the branch belongs in advance_wave, not _compute_difficulty). Add the matching test either way.

title: RecipeDef is unreachable: nothing loads the 4712 authored recipes, and ItemsApi.craft takes a prebuilt one
reason: ItemsApi.craft(recipe: RecipeDef, inventory) needs a caller-supplied RecipeDef, but no code anywhere in src/ or tests/ constructs or loads one, and no catalog method exists. ItemsApi is at its 12-method cap so a catalog cannot simply be appended. Every item 'sources' entry of the form craft:<recipe> therefore names an unreachable object, which is the whole of DEF-0057's acquisition half
next: Decide the catalog route first: split the items facade per the ISP rule, or move recipe loading into Crafting as a static so UI can list and craft. Until then a crafting screen can only craft a recipe handed to it
